title: Mouse highlighter draws a circle on desktop upon activation.

status.label: Ripple circle issue ready for focused fix design
status.detail: Two follow-up reports narrow the symptom to Ripple mode and the circle left at activation or mode-switch position.

judgment.rationale: The body and two comments provide a repeatable Ripple-only stuck-circle symptom, including reproduction by switching from Circle Highlight to Ripple. Current Mouse Highlighter source adds a MouseButton::None point when starting a draw session and restarts drawing after settings changes; this plausibly leaves an always-on circle, but the exact composition shape must be confirmed before implementation.
evidence: The reporter sees the intended ripple and a blue circle that remains until reboot on 0.101.2572 Preview.
A commenter says the stuck circle occurs only in Ripple mode, not Circle Highlight or Spotlight, on Settings or Win+Shift+H activation.
That commenter says switching from Circle Highlight to Ripple leaves a circle at the mode-switch cursor location.
Another commenter reports a stationary Mouse Highlighter dot after an Intel Graphics update while Crosshairs still work.
The primary report links a diagnostic ZIP; the second reporter supplied screenshots and another ZIP.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce activation and Circle-to-Ripple switching, identify the composition shape that remains, then scope a fix for stale always-on geometry.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-side visual-state fix is applicable if the current-source hypothesis is confirmed; no merged fix or active upstream fix PR was found in the reviewed thread.

proposed_fixes.title: Do not retain the always-on circle when Mouse Highlighter enters Ripple mode
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: activation or a settings-mode restart creates an always-on MouseButton::None circle while ripple mode is active, leaving it visible after the transient effect. StartDrawing creates an initial None point and settings changes restart drawing; this is not yet confirmed as the exact rendered shape.
plan: Reproduce direct Ripple activation and Circle-to-Ripple transition with the reporter’s settings; trace whether StartDrawing/AddDrawingPoint creates the circle and whether previous composition shapes are removed.
Clear or skip the always-on circle on Ripple activation/mode changes unless explicitly part of configured behavior.
Add focused regression coverage for Ripple startup and Circle-to-Ripple transition with a stationary pointer.
verification: Activate Ripple through its shortcut and Settings; verify no stationary circle remains after the ripple fades.
Switch from Circle Highlight to Ripple; verify the prior circle disappears while subsequent ripple clicks still render.
Run focused Mouse Highlighter validation and repeat Spotlight as a control.

confidence.rationale: The failure is corroborated and the activation/mode-switch path creates an initial always-on point, but the precise shape and graphics-update report need maintainer reproduction.

issue_context.summary: Ripple activation leaves a stationary circle; follow-up evidence narrows the ghost to switching from Circle Highlight into Ripple.
known_information: Primary report: PowerToys 0.101.2572 Preview; blue circle persists until reboot after activating Ripple.
Primary reporter attached a diagnostic ZIP.
A commenter first observed a stationary dot after an Intel Graphics update; Crosshairs still worked.
A second commenter says only Ripple triggers the circle, across Settings activation and Win+Shift+H; Circle Highlight and Spotlight do not.
Switching from Circle Highlight to Ripple leaves a circle at the cursor position; screenshot and diagnostic ZIP links were supplied.
Related #50194 describes the same Circle-to-Ripple stuck-circle symptom; it was closed by stale-feedback automation, not by a recorded fix.
inferences: The intended Ripple activation is running; the residual circle may be separate composition geometry.
The initial always-on point could account for the circle, but no trace proves it is the exact visual.
The Intel Graphics update may be coincidental; no causal evidence links it to this state.
issue_context.analysis: There is strong reproduction evidence and a narrow owning component. Current source creates an initial MouseButton::None point and restarts drawing for settings changes, so a maintainer can test whether that point survives Ripple transitions. The report is actionable for focused design, but implementation should wait for a composition-object trace.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live body and both comments through 2026-10-08T14:20:58Z, including the mode-specific description and attachment links.
Checked #50194: it describes the same Circle-to-Ripple visual and contains a detailed second-reporter reproduction; closure was automated for lack of follow-up, not a fix.
Inspected current upstream MouseHighlighter.cpp: StartDrawing adds an initial MouseButton::None point; ApplySettings sets ripple mode and restarts drawing when visible.
Latest reviewed MouseHighlighter.cpp history is PR #49699 (2026-08-11), which moved ripple work out of the low-level hook; no later path-specific fix was identified.

actions.label: Design Ripple circle cleanup
actions.note: Approve a focused fork-side design only after reproduction identifies the residual composition shape.

reproduce.version_requirement: 0.101.2572 Preview or a current build with the same Ripple implementation
prerequisites: Use Ripple mode with the reporter’s settings where available; otherwise record always-on color/opacity and Ripple configuration.
Observe a visible cursor position away from the taskbar.
steps: Activate Mouse Highlighter directly while Ripple mode is selected.
Click once and wait for the ripple animation to finish; note whether a blue circle remains stationary.
Switch from Circle Highlight to Ripple while the feature is active, then observe the circle at the mode-switch position.
Repeat activation through Settings and Win+Shift+H; compare with Circle Highlight and Spotlight controls.
Trace whether the remaining visual is the initial None point, a button pointer, ripple ring/glow, or stale composition state.
reproduce.expected_result: Ripple should display the configured transient effect only; no stale stationary circle should remain after activation or mode change.
setup_requirements: Record mode, always-on/left/right colors and alpha, Ripple settings, and activation path.
Capture which composition shape remains after the ripple fades.

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a current preview version, a direct activation scenario, and a PowerToys bug report ZIP. The lightweight code inspection found that Mouse Highlighter creates an initial always/idle visual on activation and separate ripple/button visuals with timers and fade animations, so a controlled repro trace is needed to determine which visual remains visible and why it is not cleared.
evidence: The issue targets PowerToys 0.101.2572 Preview and the Mouse Utilities area.
The reported reproduction is to activate Mouse Highlighter with the activation shortcut.
Actual behavior says the feature activates with the expected ripple effect and also draws a blue circle on the desktop that cannot be removed without rebooting.
MouseHighlighter::StartDrawing creates an initial MouseButton::None drawing point when activation starts.
MouseHighlighter handles ripple mode with hold timers, button state, fade animations, and ClearDrawing/StopDrawing paths that can distinguish stale always-on visuals from stale click/hold visuals.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a controlled maintainer reproduction using the attached diagnostics and current Mouse Highlighter settings, then inspect whether activation leaves m_alwaysPointer, a ripple hold shape, or overlay state visible after the effect should fade.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix is likely applicable if reproduced, but the lightweight pass cannot yet distinguish whether the stuck blue circle is the activation-created always pointer, a right-button/ripple hold visual, a stale composition shape, or a settings-specific overlay state.

upstream_safety.detail: No upstream or fork issue/PR writes were made.
